newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Andean Development Bank seeks to expand LatAm role.
newsitem.headline: Andean Development Bank seeks to expand LatAm role.

text.p: The Andean Development Corporation (CAF), the financial arm of the Andean Community, approved more loans for its members in 1996 than other multilateral agencies and aims to expand its regional role over the coming years, CAF officials said.

"Over the past five years the CAF has become the main source of financing for the Andean countries, more so than the Inter-American Development Bank or World Bank," CAF president Enrique Garcia told reporters.
"In the future we want to consolidate our role as catalyst for regional integration, eventually including other countries," he added.

In 1996, CAF approved credits totaling $2.2 billion to members Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Boliva. Garcia said that the CAF had held preliminary talks to include Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay and Panama, and that Jamaica would join the organization in January.

The development agency, which expects to issue some $500 million of bonds next year to fund infrastructure and communications projects between Latin American countries, is now next to Chile "the best risk in Latin America, according to ratings agencies," Garcia said.
